paper.title: Learning the Pareto Front Using Bootstrapped Observation Samples

settings.name_in_paper: Pareto front identification for linear bandits (PFILin) - sample complexity
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Multi-objective (vector-valued, L objectives) rewards; goal is identifying the Pareto front.
unmapped: Vector-valued reward with L objectives, Y = Theta^T x + eta in R^L, components of noise may be correlated
Goal: output set containing the Pareto front with all extra arms epsilon-close to the front, w.p. >= 1-delta
Learner knows theta_max (norm bound on each objective parameter), epsilon and delta
settings.definition_quote: In period $t$, the decision-maker chooses an $a_t\in[K]$, and observes a sample of the random reward vector $\mathbf{Y}_{a_t,t}=\Theta_{\star}^{\top}x_{a_{t}}+\eta_{t}$, where $\Theta_{\star}\in\Real^{d\times L}$ is the unknown (but fixed) parameters with $\|\theta^{\langle \ell \rangle}\|_{2}\le \theta_{\max}$ ... and $\eta_{t}$ is a mean-zero, $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian random error vector

settings.name_in_paper: Pareto regret during Pareto front identification (PFILin)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Multi-objective (vector-valued) rewards; regret is Pareto regret accumulated until the PFI stopping time.
unmapped: Pareto regret: sum over t up to stopping time tau_{eps,delta} of max_{k* in Pareto front} m(a_t,k*)
Horizon is the random stopping time of a PFI algorithm meeting the success condition
settings.definition_quote: the cumulative regret $R(\tau_{\epsilon,\delta})$ of an algorithm until round $\tau_{\epsilon,\delta}$ is defined as $R(\tau_{\epsilon,\delta}):=\sum_{t=1}^{\tau_{\epsilon,\delta}}\Delta_{a_t}^{\star}:=\sum_{t=1}^{\tau_{\epsilon,\delta}}\max_{k^{\star}\in\mP_{\star}}m(a_t,k^{\star})$

algorithms.name: PFIwR (Pareto Front Identification with Regret Minimization)

symbols.sum_d: sum over k=1..d of the argument, with arms ordered by increasing required accuracy
symbols.Delta_k_eps: max{Delta_(k), epsilon}, k-th smallest required accuracy floored at epsilon

conditions: any algorithm meeting the PFI success condition with confidence delta
exists a sigma-Gaussian noise distribution (hard instance)

source.label: thm:lower_bound
source.quote: Fix $\epsilon>0$, and let $\Delta_{(k),\epsilon}:=\max\{\Delta_{(k)},\epsilon\}$. Suppose the set of context vectors $\mX$ spans $\Real^{d}$ and $\|\Parameter{\ell}\|_{0} = d$, for all $\ell \in [L]$. Then, for any $\delta\in(0,1/4)$ and $\sigma>0$, there exist a $\sigma$-Gaussian distribution for the i.i.d. noise sequence such that any algorithm requires at least $(\sigma^{2}/3)\sum_{k=1}^{d}\Delta_{(k),\epsilon}^{-2} \log(3L/4\delta)$ rounds to meet the success condition

results.notes: Statement says sigma-Gaussian noise though proof constructs bounded two-point noise; recorded as sub-Gaussian setting. Generalizes Auer et al. 2016.

symbols.sum_d: sum over k=1..d of the argument, arms ordered by increasing required accuracy
symbols.T_gamma: initial exploration length 8C d^3(1+log(4C d^3 sqrt(2d)/(e sqrt(delta)))), C = 6*75^2

source.label: thm:sample
source.quote: Fix $\epsilon>0$ and $\delta \in (0,1)$. Let $\Delta_{(k),\epsilon} = \max\{\Delta_{(k)},\epsilon\}$ ... Then the stopping time $\tau_{\epsilon,\delta}$ of \texttt{PFIwR} is bounded above by $\max\{O( \sum_{k=1}^{d}\frac{(\theta_{\max}+\sigma)^{2}}{\Delta_{(k),\epsilon}^{2}}\log\frac{(\theta_{\max}+\sigma)dL}{\Delta_{(k),\epsilon}\delta}),T_{\gamma}\}$

results.notes: theta_max mapped to S. Probability not stated explicitly in theorem; implied on the 1-delta success event. The appendix restatement (Theorem B.9) gives a different expression O(sum_k d/Delta_(k),eps^2 log(dL/(Delta_eps^2 delta))); main-text version recorded.

symbols.Delta_1_eps: max{Delta_(1), epsilon}, smallest required accuracy floored at epsilon
symbols.Delta_eps_star: max{epsilon, min over Pareto-suboptimal arms of Delta_k^star}

conditions: regret accumulated up to the stopping time tau_{eps,delta}

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: The cumulative Pareto regret of \texttt{PFIwR}, $R(\tau_{\epsilon,\delta})=\bar{O}\Big(\theta_{\max}d^3\log\frac{\theta_{\max}d\sigma}{\delta\Delta_{(1),\epsilon}}+\frac{\theta_{\max}d\sigma}{\Delta_{\epsilon}^{\star}}\log\frac{\theta_{\max}d\sigma}{\Delta_{\epsilon}^{\star}\delta}\Big)$ with probability at least $1-\delta$, where $\bar{O}$ ignores $\log\log(\cdot)$ terms.

results.notes: Paper's O-bar ignores loglog terms; recorded as O. Comparator is the Pareto front (Pareto regret), mapped to best_fixed_action approximately. Proof ends with sigma^2 in the second term while statement has sigma; statement recorded. Theorem also gives instantaneous regret <= 2 max beta_{j,t-1} (not recorded separately).

symbols.Delta_eps_star: max{epsilon, min over Pareto-suboptimal arms of Delta_k^star}

conditions: for any PFI algorithm that satisfies PFI success condition (1) with failure probability delta
exists a sigma-sub-Gaussian i.i.d. noise distribution (hard instance)

source.label: thm:regret_lower_bound
source.quote: Suppose the set of context vectors $\mathcal{X}$ span $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\min_{\ell \in [L]}\|\theta_{\star}^{\langle \ell \rangle}\|_0 = d$. Then, for any $\delta \in (0,1/4)$ and $\sigma>0$, there exists a $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian distribution for the i.i.d. noise sequence such that for any PFI algorithms that satisfies PFI success condition (1) with failure probability $\delta$, $R(\tau_{\epsilon,\delta}) \ge \frac{\sqrt{3}d\sigma}{8\Delta_{\epsilon}^{\star}} \log \frac{1}{4\delta}$.

results.notes: Statement does not specify expectation vs probability; proof invokes an expected-regret Omega(sqrt(dT)) bound, so quantity regret_unspecified with probability set to expectation. Proof argument is loose.
